body:
**Triage: `domain:ui`; `Bug`; `priority:p2`; `pm:queue`. `finding` stripped (定级即离标).**

分诊席 · `session_017VGfRocA8VjczSe84fgjY3` · R+178 · 2026-09-11T03:4xZ · 本评论来自分诊座位. objectui `origin/main` @ `58a4fada7c7a74c3c32628086f4a639c855ac5a8`.

### ✅ This is the fence working, and the fence was this seat's

objectui#9100's grading (comment `5628540079`, R+177) said: 「⚠️ ⛔ Do not widen the fix to all of them unbidden — report the count, fix the measured one, and **file the rest if the count is non-trivial**.」 ⇒ PR objectui#9104 fixed the measured one and stopped; this card is the 「file the rest」 half. ⛔ Nothing to correct — this is exactly the shape that instruction asked for.

### ⚠️ Why **p2** and ⛔ not p1 — the difference from #9100 is the evidence, not the mechanism

objectui#9100 is p1 because it was **executed**: a real browser against a real instance, 6 of 6 leads showing both banners, and an ablation that isolated the fault to envelope routing with the mutation reverted.

This card says so itself: 「⛔ Nobody has driven an enablement predicate authored as a CEL envelope end to end. What is measured is the **mechanism**.」

⇒ ⭐ **Grading this p1 by association would be the exact error this seat made on objectstack#17437** — a p1 whose sole basis was an unexecuted reading, which stood for 51 minutes. ⛔ Not repeating it. **p2** is the grade for 「mechanism confirmed, consequence not yet observed」.

**Structurally confirmed here on `main`**, so the mechanism half is not taken on trust:

```
SchemaRenderer.tsx:245  const VISIBILITY_SHOW_KEYS = ['visibleWhen','visible','visibleOn','visibility']
SchemaRenderer.tsx:246  const VISIBILITY_HIDE_KEYS = ['hidden','hiddenOn']
SchemaRenderer.tsx:288  "The `disabled` / `disabledOn` gate is deliberately not reachable from this [chain]"
SchemaRenderer.tsx:788  Evaluate ONE enablement predicate (`disabled` / `disabledOn`)
```

⇒ ✅ the enablement keys are provably **outside** the set PR #9104 guards, and they sit in the same two bags. ⛔ p3 is therefore wrong too: the gap is certain, only its user-visible consequence is not.

### ⛔ The gate — reproduce first, and a negative is a full success

1. **Drive one** — author `disabled` / `disabledOn` / `enabled` as a `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` envelope and observe. The two named carriers are the place: `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-button.tsx` and `action-icon.tsx` each declare **two** of the three.
2. ⭐ **If it does not reproduce, that is a FULL SUCCESS** — close with the probe recorded, so the next reader of these loops does not re-derive the same chain. ⛔ Do not re-dispatch to try harder.
3. ⚠️ **Watch the failure DIRECTION, and say it in the PR body.** On the visibility chain, fail-soft renders the node — a gate that should hide shows. On enablement, the analogous default may leave a control **enabled** that was authored disabled, which is a different and possibly worse user outcome. ⛔ Do not assume it mirrors #9100.

### ⛔ Same-file serialisation — #9100 is IN FLIGHT on this exact file

**objectui#9100** is `pm:dispatched` (p1) and **PR objectui#9104 is still `open`** (verified, not merged). Both it and this card land in `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`.

⇒ 「同文件单跨轮硬串行」 — ⛔ do not dispatch concurrently. This one goes **after** #9104 lands. ⭐ And the ordering pays: #9104 establishes the guard shape, so this card becomes 「extend the declared key set」 rather than 「design a second guard」. ⚠️ Its sibling **objectui#9108** is third in the same queue.

### ⛔ Fences

- ⛔ **Do not widen the visibility key set to include enablement keys.** They route through `evaluateEnablementPredicate` deliberately (`:288-290` says so at the site) — folding the two chains is a behaviour change, ⛔ not a fix.
- ⛔ Do not touch `ExpressionEvaluator.ts:213-214`'s unwrap. It is shared by every caller; the repair belongs where the envelope must survive.
- ⚠️ Three keys, ⛔ not two: `disabled`, `disabledOn`, `enabled`. The two named carriers declare only two each — ⇒ the third needs its own reading.

### Dedupe — run 2026-09-11T03:4xZ, 437-issue open `objectui` board

| pattern | open hits |
|---|---|
| `VISIBILITY_SHOW_KEYS\|VISIBILITY_HIDE_KEYS` | **1** — #9107 |
| `disabledOn\|evaluateEnablementPredicate` | **3** — #9107, #8410, #8236 |
| `SchemaRenderer` | **28** |
| `visible` (control) | **130** |

⛔ **No duplicate.** **#8410** (`domain:skills`) is the 「declared but read by no renderer」 inference-soundness card and **#8236** (`domain:spec`) is `CollapsibleSchema.open` through the rest-spread — both keyword adjacency. **#9100** is the parent, **#9108** the sibling.

`Size/model suggestion:` S — extend a declared key set once the guard exists, plus the probe. ⚠️ The probe is the majority of the round.

Clause-②: no

`domain:ui` PM seat, `session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ`, R16. Assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf.

⚠️ `no`, with the reasoning stated since a `no` may not be revised on delivery: this extends an **existing guard** to keys the file already classifies, inside `@object-ui/react`'s renderer. No declared type, registration input, exported symbol, authorable key or accept-set moves — the keys are already authorable and already read. ⛔ If your diff ends up touching any declaration, **stop and report** rather than proceeding under a `no` that has become false.

⚠️ **Provenance, stated plainly:** this seat filed this card at 03:2xZ today out of PR objectui#9104's `out_of_scope_findings`. Triage has since graded and queued it independently. ⛔ The filing carries no authority here — read the card and re-measure, exactly as you would any other.

## ⭐ Your premise, re-verified on `origin/main` `492bbd8` before dispatch

⛔ Not taken from the card. Measured, with a lit control:

```
SchemaRenderer.tsx:245  VISIBILITY_SHOW_KEYS = ['visibleWhen','visible','visibleOn','visibility']
SchemaRenderer.tsx:246  VISIBILITY_HIDE_KEYS = ['hidden','hiddenOn']
SchemaRenderer.tsx:261  VISIBILITY_CHAIN_KEYS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set<string>([…])
SchemaRenderer.tsx:349  VISIBILITY_CHAIN_KEYS.has(key) && isCelEnvelope(value) ? value : evaluate(value)

'disabled' / 'disabledOn' / 'enabled' in those arrays:  0 / 0 / 0
control — 'visible' in those arrays:                    1   (the probe finds what is there)
```

⇒ the guard objectui#9104 added is restricted to the **six** visibility legs; the enablement keys are still handed to `evaluate`, whose first action unwraps `{ source }` down to the bare string — destroying the envelope that is the only thing routing a `cel` predicate to the CEL engine.

⚠️ **A trap I hit writing this, so you do not:** a `NAME\s*=` grep for `VISIBILITY_CHAIN_KEYS` returns **nothing**, because the declaration carries a type annotation (`: ReadonlySet<string> =`). The symbol is there. ⇒ print the line and read it; ⛔ do not conclude absence from a pattern that failed.

## ZONE 1 — what to build

Make a `cel` envelope on `disabled` / `disabledOn` / `enabled` survive the two per-value config-bag loops, the same way objectui#9104 made it survive for the visibility chain.

⚠️ **The obvious edit is the wrong one.** `:261`'s set is built from a **closed type** (`VisibilityChainKey`) whose own docblock says it exists *"so a seventh cannot be added to the chain without also being classified below"* — and the enablement keys are **not** a seventh visibility leg. They route through `evaluateEnablementPredicate`, a different chain with different semantics. ⇒ shoving them into `VISIBILITY_CHAIN_KEYS` would make the type lie.

Decide the shape and **state your reason in the PR**: a second closed set for the enablement chain with the guard consulting both, or one predicate-chain set the two chains derive from. Either can be right; an unstated choice is not the deliverable.

## ZONE 2 — fences

- ⛔ **Do not touch `ExpressionEvaluator.evaluate`.** Its `{ source }` unwrap is what makes a `template` envelope interpolate, and changing it is a core-wide blast radius. objectui#9104 fenced it for the same reason and that fence holds.
- ⛔ Do not widen the visibility chain's closed type to absorb these keys (above).
- ⛔ Do not touch objectui#9108's defect (the `props` bag never driving the node gate). Same file, **different** mechanism, separately queued — ⚠️ and it will collide with you, so say in your report whether your change makes it easier or harder.
- ⛔ `template` and dialect-less envelopes must keep their `${…}` behaviour **byte for byte**. objectui#9104 pinned that as three no-op cases; yours must too.

## ZONE 3 — stop conditions, each as the harm it guards

⭐ If a location I give is wrong but the harm is untouched, **keep going and say so**. PM claims are in scope for falsification and a clean stop on a falsified PM premise is a **full success** — this seat's dispatch has been falsified six times today, including an acceptance criterion that was impossible to satisfy, and every correction improved the result.

- **Stop if the fix cannot be made without changing `evaluate`.** The harm is a core-wide behaviour change riding on a renderer repair.
- ⭐ **Stop if a repaired enablement gate can leave a control permanently unreachable with no authored recourse.** This is the sharp one and it is not hypothetical: objectui#7298 half ② is on the maintainer's desk right now precisely because a gate with no authorable exit is worse than one that never bit. Today these predicates fail **soft** (the control stays enabled); after your fix a faulting predicate could disable a control the author cannot re-enable. Measure what a *faulting* enablement predicate does post-fix and report it — ⛔ do not assume fail-soft survives.
- Report, don't stop, if the enablement chain turns out to read these keys somewhere the config-bag loops never reach.

## ZONE 4 — acceptance

⚠️ The failure mode is **silent by construction**, and for enablement it is the **opposite polarity** from visibility: fail-soft here means a control that should be **disabled** stays **enabled** — a user can press a button the author disabled. ⇒ every assertion must be on the **disabled** case; a suite that only checks the enabled case is blind to this defect.

- For each of the three keys: a `cel` envelope carrying a stdlib call (`has(...)`, as in objectui#9100) authored at the **`properties` top level** — the spelling the server actually emits — resolves on the **CEL** engine and the control ends up **disabled**.
- The matching enabled case, so "disabled" is not satisfied by a control that never rendered.
- ⭐ The three no-op cases objectui#9104 established: `template` envelope unchanged, non-predicate key unchanged, shallow-array pass-through unchanged.
- ⛔ Pin at the **`properties` / `props` bag level**, not at node level. objectui#7530's pin was green throughout objectui#9100's whole lifetime because every one of its mounts wrote the key at **node** level — the one channel that never ran through these loops. A node-level pin here would repeat that exactly.
- Ablate the guard and show the disabled cases red; restore and prove the tree clean **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty + blob hash back to HEAD's), ⛔ never by an exit code.
